newsitem.title: UK: Drought-hit N. Korea in "dire" state-CNN chief.
newsitem.headline: Drought-hit N. Korea in "dire" state-CNN chief.

text.p: A U.S. broadcaster on a trip to North Korea said on Wednesday the famine-hit country was in dire straits and predicted this year's rice crop could be as disastrous as the corn crop.
"The situation here is unquestionably dire," CNN International president Eason Jordan told the channel in a live link-up from the capital Pyongyang.
Two years of floods had already depleted food stocks in the secretive Stalinist state so when drought hit the country this year catastrophe beckoned.
Jordan, who said he had been given wide access during the five days he had spent in the country so far, said the drought was wreaking havoc.

He said he had been to farmland in the south earlier on Wednesday where it was clear the corn crop had been badly hit. CNN broadcast film of withered corn plants which Jordan said he had taken on Wednesday.
"There we saw the corn crop that has been lost -- 70 percent of the corn crop has been lost. 1.5 million tonnes of corn have been lost," he said.

"And unless there is rain in this country between now and October we're going to see the rice crop suffer the same fate as the corn crop...in the rice fields where there should be a foot (33 cm) of water at least, there is less than one or two inches in most cases."
Humanitarian aid groups say an estimated 80,000 children in North Korea are severely malnourished and in danger of dying from starvation and disease.

"There is an untold number of deaths. Clearly there have been some, perhaps not many, we do not have a precise number. We know the deaths are coming mostly among the young and the elderly," Jordan told CNN.
"The city and the country are largely longing for water. I was just this evening at a huge lake in southern North Korea and it was 96 percent gone, evaporated into thin air," he said.
"If there's no rain within two weeks -- and there has been no rain all summer here in North Korea -- that lake and many other lakes will simply disappear."
United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan called on Monday for countries to put aside their misgivings about North Korea to aid its victims.
U.N. officials say the situation in North Korea is worse than the famine which hit Ethiopia in the mid-1980s.
"North Korean officials and the international relief agencies' workers who I have met are pleading for help, saying they need 800,000 tonnes of food between now and the end of October," Jordan said.
CNN is a subsidiary of Time Warner Inc.
